title: The moment felt right.
paragraphs:
The moment felt right.
But right doesn’t always mean righteous.

Rebekah stood in the quiet tension between promise and patience—
a place many of us know too well.

God had already spoken.
The older would serve the younger.
The blessing was destined for Jacob.

But here’s what most people don’t realize…
knowing God’s promise is not the same as trusting God’s timing.
And that’s where everything began to fracture.

Isaac was old.
Blind.
Ready to release the blessing.

Esau moved first.
Naturally. Traditionally. Expected.

But Rebekah…
she intervened.

Not with prayer.
Not with surrender.
But with strategy.
Deception was born in the shadow of a promise.

She dressed Jacob in Esau’s garments.
Covered his smooth skin with goat hair.
Prepared a meal that would fool a father’s fading senses.

And in that moment—
what God intended to fulfill through sovereignty…
Rebekah forced through manipulation.
Read that again.

This wasn’t just a family mistake.
This was a spiritual warning.

Because if we’re honest—
you’ve done this too.

You saw what God showed you…
but instead of waiting, you worked it out your own way.

You rushed the relationship.
Forced the opportunity.
Manipulated the outcome.
Why?
Because waiting felt like losing.

But here’s the truth most people avoid:
When you rush God’s will, you inherit consequences God never intended.

Jacob received the blessing. Yes.
But at what cost?

A broken family.
A fleeing son.
A grieving mother who would never see him again.

Rebekah got the outcome…
but lost the peace.
Because partial obedience is still disobedience.
And here’s the breaking point:

The issue was never the promise.
The issue was sin.

Control.
Fear.
Unbelief.
Trying to “help God” is often just a disguised refusal to trust Him.
And that’s where every human story collides with the Gospel.

Because you cannot fix what sin has broken.
You cannot redeem what manipulation has corrupted.
But Jesus can.
And He did.

Where Rebekah rushed—
Christ waited.

Where we deceive—
Christ is truth.

Where we take control—
Christ surrendered fully to the Father’s will… even to death on a cross.

Not to manage outcomes—
but to redeem souls.
This is the part everything turns.
Because your story doesn’t end in your mistake.

Through Jesus Christ:
Sin is exposed → repentance is offered → grace is given → redemption is secured.

Not by your effort.
Not by your timing.
But by His finished work.
If this found you, it’s not by accident.

There’s a deeper layer to this—
one most people never reach because they stop at the story instead of surrendering in the Spirit.
